text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Opposition parties are attacking the government after receiving letters from Gerhard Praschak, former chief of clearing bank Kontrollbank, who comitted suicide over the weekend blaming political influence in the banking sector.
- Klaus Bachler, current head of Vienna's Volksoper, will succeed Burgtheater director Claus Peymann, whose contract will end in 1999.
- Regional utility company EVN demands national grid company Verbund should sell its electricity cheaper to be more competitive when the Austrian market is liberalised.
- Erich Hampel, former chief of postal savings bank PSK, has been formally elected as Creditanstalt's new chief executive.
- Insurer EA-Generali's Hungarian subsidiaries have raised their premiums by a third to about 1.88 billion schillings.

- The Foreign Ministry has said it would investigate the involvement of former ministry officials in the case of the release of the alleged murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989. However the report will not be ready for a special parliamentary session on the issue on May 6.
- The European Union has said it would not accept the government's plan to exclude the state-owned loss-making road financing company Asfinag from the budget in order to meet the Maastricht criteria.

- Chamber of Economy chief Leopold Maderthaner says the European single currency euro will secure jobs and that further austerity measures will be introduced if unions try to stop Austria participating in European Economic and Monetary Union.

- EVN chief Rudolf Gruber expects the European Union not to oppose a planned risk-sharing programme of Austria's electricity businesses in order to remain competitive in a liberalised market. He repeated the regional utility firms' offer to take over the state's 26 percent stake in Verbund.
- Vienna is the sixth-richest region within the EU.
- Fireproof maker Radex-Heraklith reported a pre-tax loss of 91 million schillings in the first quarter of 1997, from 55 million in the year ago period.
- Microchip-maker AMS reported first quarter pre-tax losses of 8.5 million schillings. However the company expects profits in 1997.
- Kurt Noesslinger, former chief of postal savings bank PSK, is to become the bank's acting chief after chief executive Erich Hampel was appointed head of Creditanstalt.
- Gerhard Praschak accused Bank Austria and Creditanstalt, major share-holders in Kontrollbank, of manipulating the bank's profits.
